jesus_905.name: Jesus
jesus_905.who: The Son of God and promised Messiah, born of Mary, who died for sinners and rose again.
key: He was born of the virgin Mary in Bethlehem and laid in a manger (Luke 2).
He was baptized by John and then tempted by the devil in the wilderness (Matthew 3–4).
He preached the kingdom of God, called disciples, taught, and healed many throughout Galilee (Mark 1).
He was crucified under Pontius Pilate and buried in a new tomb (John 19).
He rose from the dead on the third day and later ascended into heaven (Luke 24).

israel_682.name: Jacob
israel_682.who: Son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel by God, whose twelve sons became the tribes of Israel.
key: He was born holding Esau's heel and later bought Esau's birthright for stew (Genesis 25).
He deceived his blind father Isaac to receive the blessing meant for Esau (Genesis 27).
Fleeing Esau, he dreamed of a ladder to heaven and received God's promise at Bethel (Genesis 28).
He served Laban and married Leah and Rachel (Genesis 29).
He wrestled with God at Peniel and was renamed Israel (Genesis 32).

david_994.name: David
david_994.who: Shepherd from Bethlehem who became Israel's greatest king, a psalmist, and ancestor of the Messiah.
key: Samuel anointed the young shepherd David as the next king of Israel (1 Samuel 16).
He killed the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and a stone (1 Samuel 17).
He became king over all Israel and made Jerusalem his capital (2 Samuel 5).
God promised that David's throne and dynasty would be established forever (2 Samuel 7).
He committed adultery with Bathsheba and arranged Uriah's death, then was confronted by Nathan (2 Samuel 11–12).

moses_2108.name: Moses
moses_2108.who: Hebrew prophet and lawgiver whom God used to lead Israel out of Egypt and give the law at Sinai.
key: As a baby he was hidden in a basket and adopted by Pharaoh's daughter (Exodus 2).
God called him from a burning bush to deliver Israel from Egypt (Exodus 3).
He led the Israelites through the Red Sea on dry ground (Exodus 14).
He received the Ten Commandments and the law from God on Mount Sinai (Exodus 20).
Barred from entering Canaan, he viewed the land from Mount Nebo and died there (Deuteronomy 34).

aaron_1.name: Aaron
aaron_1.who: Older brother of Moses, his spokesman before Pharaoh, and the first high priest of Israel.
key: God appointed Aaron to speak for Moses and sent him to meet his brother (Exodus 4).
Before Pharaoh, Aaron's staff became a serpent and swallowed the magicians' staffs (Exodus 7).
While Moses was on Mount Sinai, Aaron made the golden calf for the people (Exodus 32).
He and his sons were consecrated as Israel's priests (Leviticus 8).
He died on Mount Hor, and his son Eleazar succeeded him as priest (Numbers 20).

abraham_58.name: Abraham
abraham_58.who: Patriarch called by God to go to Canaan, with whom God made a covenant to bless all nations.
key: God called Abram to leave his country and promised to make him a great nation (Genesis 12).
He believed the Lord, and God counted it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15).
God renamed him Abraham and gave circumcision as the sign of the covenant (Genesis 17).
In his old age, Sarah bore him the promised son Isaac (Genesis 21).
He obeyed God's command to offer Isaac, and God provided a ram instead (Genesis 22).

solomon_2762.name: Solomon
solomon_2762.who: Son of David and Bathsheba who succeeded David as king, famed for wisdom and for building the temple.
key: Born to David and Bathsheba, he was also named Jedidiah by the Lord through Nathan (2 Samuel 12).
He was anointed king to succeed his father David (1 Kings 1).
He asked God for wisdom, and God also gave him riches and honor (1 Kings 3).
He built the temple in Jerusalem and dedicated it with prayer (1 Kings 8).
His many foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, so the kingdom was divided after him (1 Kings 11).

saul_2478.name: Saul
saul_2478.who: Son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin, anointed by Samuel as Israel's first king.
key: Samuel anointed Saul, who was later chosen by lot as king (1 Samuel 10).
He offered a sacrifice himself instead of waiting for Samuel, and was rebuked (1 Samuel 13).
He spared King Agag and the best livestock, and God rejected him as king (1 Samuel 15).
Jealous of David, he repeatedly tried to kill him (1 Samuel 18–26).
He consulted a medium at En-dor, then died in battle on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 28–31).

holy_spirit_7400.name: Holy Spirit
holy_spirit_7400.who: The Spirit of God, the third person of the Trinity, active in creation, inspiring prophets, and indwelling believers.
key: The Spirit of God hovered over the waters at creation (Genesis 1).
The Spirit came upon judges, kings, and prophets to empower them for God's work (Judges 6).
The Spirit descended on Jesus like a dove at his baptism (Matthew 3).
Jesus promised to send the Spirit as Helper to teach and guide his disciples (John 14).
The Spirit was poured out on the believers at Pentecost (Acts 2).

judah_1751.name: Judah
judah_1751.who: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Judah and of King David.
key: He was born to Leah, who named him in praise of the Lord (Genesis 29).
He proposed selling his brother Joseph to traders rather than killing him (Genesis 37).
He fathered the twins Perez and Zerah by his daughter-in-law Tamar (Genesis 38).
In Egypt he offered himself as a slave in place of Benjamin (Genesis 44).
Jacob blessed him, saying the scepter would not depart from Judah (Genesis 49).

joseph_1710.name: Joseph
joseph_1710.who: Favored son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into slavery by his brothers, who rose to rule Egypt.
key: Jacob's favorite, he dreamed of ruling his brothers, who sold him into slavery (Genesis 37).
Falsely accused by Potiphar's wife, he was thrown into prison (Genesis 39).
He interpreted Pharaoh's dreams and was made ruler over Egypt (Genesis 41).
He revealed himself to his brothers and brought Jacob's family to Egypt (Genesis 45).
He told his brothers that God meant their evil for good, then died in Egypt (Genesis 50).

joshua_1727.name: Joshua
joshua_1727.who: Son of Nun, Moses' assistant and successor, who led Israel into the Promised Land.
key: He led Israel's army to victory over Amalek while Moses held up his hands (Exodus 17).
With Caleb, he was one of two spies who urged Israel to trust God (Numbers 13–14).
He was commissioned to succeed Moses as Israel's leader (Deuteronomy 31).
He led Israel across the Jordan and conquered Jericho (Joshua 3–6).
Before his death, he called Israel to serve the Lord alone (Joshua 24).

paul_2479.name: Paul
paul_2479.who: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecuted the church, then became an apostle to the Gentiles and wrote many New Testament letters.
key: As a young man named Saul, he approved of the stoning of Stephen (Acts 7).
The risen Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus, and he was converted (Acts 9).
Sent out with Barnabas, he preached the gospel to Jews and Gentiles in many cities (Acts 13–14).
He was arrested in Jerusalem and appealed to Caesar (Acts 21–25).
After a shipwreck, he reached Rome and preached there under house arrest (Acts 27–28).

peter_2745.name: Peter
peter_2745.who: Galilean fisherman, brother of Andrew, who became a leading apostle of Jesus and preached at Pentecost.
key: Jesus called him from his fishing nets to follow him (Matthew 4).
He confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God (Matthew 16).
He denied knowing Jesus three times on the night of Jesus' arrest (Mark 14).
The risen Jesus restored him and told him to feed his sheep (John 21).
He preached at Pentecost and later brought the gospel to the Gentile Cornelius (Acts 2; Acts 10).

ephraim_1206.name: Ephraim
ephraim_1206.who: Younger son of Joseph born in Egypt, ancestor of the tribe of Ephraim, a leading northern tribe.
key: Joseph named him Ephraim because God had made him fruitful in Egypt (Genesis 41).
Jacob crossed his hands and blessed Ephraim above his older brother Manasseh (Genesis 48).
After some of his sons were killed by men of Gath, he mourned many days (1 Chronicles 7).

benjamin_463.name: Benjamin
benjamin_463.who: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, ancestor of the tribe of Benjamin.
key: Rachel died giving birth to him; she named him Ben-oni, but Jacob called him Benjamin (Genesis 35).
Jacob kept him home when his brothers first went to Egypt for grain (Genesis 42).
Joseph's silver cup was planted in his sack to test the brothers (Genesis 44).
Jacob blessed him as a ravenous wolf (Genesis 49).

esau_1216.name: Esau
esau_1216.who: Older twin brother of Jacob, son of Isaac and Rebekah, and ancestor of the Edomites.
key: Born first of twins, he later sold his birthright to Jacob for a meal (Genesis 25).
Jacob received Isaac's blessing instead of him, and Esau planned to kill Jacob (Genesis 27).
Years later he ran to meet Jacob and embraced him in reconciliation (Genesis 33).
He settled in the hill country of Seir and became the father of the Edomites (Genesis 36).

moab_2103.name: Moab
moab_2103.who: Son of Lot by his older daughter and ancestor of the Moabites, the nation east of the Dead Sea.
key: He was born to Lot's older daughter after she made her father drunk in a cave (Genesis 19).
His descendants, the Moabites, became a nation that often opposed Israel (Numbers 22).
Ruth, an ancestor of David, came from the land of Moab (Ruth 1).

pharaoh_2331.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2331.who: The king of Egypt at the exodus, who refused to free Israel until God struck Egypt with plagues.
key: When Moses and Aaron asked him to let Israel go, he made their labor harder (Exodus 5).
He hardened his heart as God sent plague after plague on Egypt (Exodus 7–10).
After the death of Egypt's firstborn, he told the Israelites to leave (Exodus 12).
He pursued Israel, and his army drowned in the Red Sea (Exodus 14).
Paul says God raised him up to display divine power (Romans 9).

jeremiah_853.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_853.who: Prophet from a priestly family who warned Judah of judgment before and during Babylon's conquest of Jerusalem.
key: God called him as a prophet while he was still young (Jeremiah 1).
Pashhur the priest beat him and put him in the stocks (Jeremiah 20).
During the siege of Jerusalem, he bought a field as a sign of future restoration (Jeremiah 32).
He was thrown into a muddy cistern and rescued by Ebed-melech (Jeremiah 38).
After Jerusalem fell, he was taken to Egypt against his warning (Jeremiah 43).

isaac_616.name: Isaac
isaac_616.who: The promised son of Abraham and Sarah, father of Jacob and Esau, and heir of God's covenant.
key: He was born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age, as God had promised (Genesis 21).
Abraham bound him on an altar, but God provided a ram in his place (Genesis 22).
He married Rebekah, whom Abraham's servant brought from his relatives (Genesis 24).
Old and blind, he was deceived into blessing Jacob instead of Esau (Genesis 27).
He died at an old age and was buried by Esau and Jacob (Genesis 35).

samuel_2469.name: Samuel
samuel_2469.who: Prophet, priest, and last judge of Israel, who anointed both Saul and David as king.
key: Born in answer to Hannah's prayer, he was dedicated to serve the Lord at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1).
As a boy, he heard the Lord call him by name at night (1 Samuel 3).
He led Israel in repentance, and God routed the Philistines at Mizpah (1 Samuel 7).
He anointed Saul as Israel's first king (1 Samuel 10).
He anointed the young David as king in Bethlehem (1 Samuel 16).

joab_1617.name: Joab
joab_1617.who: Son of David's sister Zeruiah and the commander of David's army.
key: He led the attack on Jerusalem and became chief commander (1 Chronicles 11).
He murdered Abner in revenge for his brother Asahel's death (2 Samuel 3).
At David's order, he placed Uriah where he would be killed in battle (2 Samuel 11).
He killed Absalom against David's orders (2 Samuel 18).
After supporting Adonijah, he was executed at Solomon's command (1 Kings 2).

hezekiah_1512.name: Hezekiah
hezekiah_1512.who: Faithful king of Judah, son of Ahaz, who trusted the Lord when Assyria threatened Jerusalem.
key: He removed idols and broke the bronze serpent Moses had made (2 Kings 18).
He invited all Israel to Jerusalem to keep a great Passover (2 Chronicles 30).
When Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem, he prayed, and an angel struck the Assyrian army (2 Kings 19).
When he was deathly ill, God added fifteen years to his life (2 Kings 20).
He showed his treasures to Babylonian envoys, and Isaiah foretold exile to Babylon (Isaiah 39).

manasseh_1928.name: Manasseh
manasseh_1928.who: Firstborn son of Joseph born in Egypt, ancestor of the tribe of Manasseh.
key: Joseph named him Manasseh because God had made him forget his hardship (Genesis 41).
Jacob blessed him but placed his younger brother Ephraim ahead of him (Genesis 48).
His descendants received land on both sides of the Jordan (Joshua 17).

elijah_1131.name: Elijah
elijah_1131.who: Prophet from Tishbe who confronted King Ahab and Baal worship in Israel and was taken up to heaven.
key: He announced a drought, was fed by ravens, and raised a widow's son (1 Kings 17).
On Mount Carmel, God answered his prayer with fire, defeating the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18).
He confronted Ahab for seizing Naboth's vineyard (1 Kings 21).
He was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind as Elisha watched (2 Kings 2).
He appeared with Moses at Jesus' transfiguration (Luke 9).

absalom_59.name: Absalom
absalom_59.who: Son of David by Maacah who rebelled against his father and tried to seize the throne.
key: He killed his half-brother Amnon for violating his sister Tamar, then fled (2 Samuel 13).
Joab arranged his return to Jerusalem and reconciliation with David (2 Samuel 14).
He won the hearts of Israel and declared himself king at Hebron (2 Samuel 15).
Caught by his head in an oak tree, he was killed by Joab (2 Samuel 18).
David mourned him deeply, crying out for his son (2 Samuel 18).

john_1676.name: John the Baptist
john_1676.who: Prophet, son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, who prepared the way for Jesus and baptized him.
key: An angel announced his birth to his father Zechariah in the temple (Luke 1).
He preached repentance in the wilderness and baptized people in the Jordan (Matthew 3).
He baptized Jesus and pointed to him as the Lamb of God (John 1).
From prison he sent disciples to ask Jesus if he was the coming one (Luke 7).
Herod had him beheaded at the request of Herodias's daughter (Mark 6).

nebuchadnezzar_2167.name: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar_2167.who: King of Babylon who conquered Judah, destroyed Jerusalem, and was humbled by the God of Israel.
key: He besieged Jerusalem and carried King Jehoiachin and many others to Babylon (2 Kings 24).
His army burned the temple and Jerusalem after a long siege (2 Kings 25).
Daniel interpreted his dream of a great statue (Daniel 2).
He threw three Jewish men into a fiery furnace, but God delivered them (Daniel 3).
Humbled to live like an animal, he later praised the Most High God (Daniel 4).

canaan_914.name: Canaan
canaan_914.who: Son of Ham and grandson of Noah, ancestor of the Canaanite peoples whose land bore his name.
key: Noah cursed Canaan after Ham saw his father's nakedness (Genesis 9).
His descendants included Sidon, Heth, the Jebusites, the Amorites, and other peoples (Genesis 10).
God promised the land of Canaan to Abraham's offspring (Genesis 17).

jonathan_1692.name: Jonathan
jonathan_1692.who: Eldest son of King Saul, a brave warrior, and David's loyal friend.
key: With only his armor-bearer, he attacked a Philistine garrison, and God gave victory (1 Samuel 14).
He made a covenant with David and gave him his robe and weapons (1 Samuel 18).
He warned David of Saul's intent to kill him using arrows as a signal (1 Samuel 20).
He was killed with his father in battle on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31).
David mourned him in a lament for Saul and Jonathan (2 Samuel 1).

jeroboam_872.name: Jeroboam
jeroboam_872.who: Son of Nebat and first king of the northern kingdom of Israel, who led it into idolatry.
key: The prophet Ahijah tore his cloak and promised Jeroboam ten tribes (1 Kings 11).
When the northern tribes rejected Rehoboam, they made Jeroboam king (1 Kings 12).
He set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan to keep people from Jerusalem (1 Kings 12).
A man of God denounced his altar at Bethel, and Jeroboam's hand withered (1 Kings 13).
Ahijah foretold the destruction of his house because of his sin (1 Kings 14).

ahab_113.name: Ahab
ahab_113.who: Son of Omri and king of Israel who, with his wife Jezebel, promoted Baal worship and opposed Elijah.
key: He married Jezebel and built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria (1 Kings 16).
Elijah defeated the prophets of Baal before him on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18).
God gave him victories over Ben-hadad of Syria (1 Kings 20).
Jezebel had Naboth killed so Ahab could take his vineyard (1 Kings 21).
He disguised himself in battle at Ramoth-gilead but was killed by a random arrow (1 Kings 22).

daniel_975.name: Daniel
daniel_975.who: Young Judean taken to Babylon who served faithfully in royal courts and received visions from God.
key: Taken to Babylon, he refused the king's food and was renamed Belteshazzar (Daniel 1).
God revealed to him Nebuchadnezzar's dream and its meaning (Daniel 2).
He interpreted the handwriting on the wall for Belshazzar (Daniel 5).
Thrown into the lions' den for praying to God, he was kept safe (Daniel 6).
He received visions of four beasts and the Son of Man (Daniel 7).

reuben_2429.name: Reuben
reuben_2429.who: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Reuben.
key: He was born to Leah, the first of Jacob's sons (Genesis 29).
He slept with his father's concubine Bilhah (Genesis 35).
He persuaded his brothers not to kill Joseph and planned to rescue him (Genesis 37).
He offered his own sons as a pledge for Benjamin's safe return (Genesis 42).
Jacob said he would lose his preeminence because he defiled his father's bed (Genesis 49).

jehoshaphat_808.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_808.who: Son of Asa and a godly king of Judah who sought the Lord and taught his law.
key: He sent officials and Levites to teach the Book of the Law in Judah (2 Chronicles 17).
He allied with Ahab at Ramoth-gilead and narrowly escaped death (1 Kings 22).
He appointed judges and urged them to judge in the fear of the Lord (2 Chronicles 19).
Facing a vast army, he prayed, and God gave victory as Judah sang praises (2 Chronicles 20).
He joined Israel's king against Moab and sought counsel from Elisha (2 Kings 3).

levi_1820.name: Levi
levi_1820.who: Third son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the Levites, Israel's priestly tribe.
key: He was born to Leah, who hoped her husband would now be attached to her (Genesis 29).
With Simeon, he killed the men of Shechem to avenge their sister Dinah (Genesis 34).
Jacob rebuked Levi and Simeon for their violent anger (Genesis 49).
His descendants were set apart to serve at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).

dan_973.name: Dan
dan_973.who: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Dan.
key: Rachel named him Dan, saying God had judged her and given her a son (Genesis 30).
Jacob blessed him, saying Dan would judge his people (Genesis 49).
His tribe later moved north, captured Laish, and renamed it Dan (Judges 18).

pharaoh_2329.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2329.who: The king of Egypt in Joseph's day, who made Joseph ruler over Egypt and welcomed Jacob's family.
key: He imprisoned his chief cupbearer and baker, who met Joseph in prison (Genesis 40).
Joseph interpreted his dreams, and he set Joseph over all Egypt (Genesis 41).
He invited Joseph's family to come and live in Egypt (Genesis 45).
He gave Jacob's family the land of Goshen, and Jacob blessed him (Genesis 47).

eleazar_1062.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1062.who: Son of Aaron who succeeded his father as Israel's high priest.
key: He was placed over the leaders of the Levites and the care of the sanctuary (Numbers 3).
On Mount Hor, Aaron's priestly garments were put on him before Aaron died (Numbers 20).
He commissioned Joshua with Moses before the congregation (Numbers 27).
With Joshua, he distributed the land of Canaan among the tribes (Joshua 14).
He died and was buried in the hill country of Ephraim (Joshua 24).

balaam_593.name: Balaam
balaam_593.who: Son of Beor, a diviner hired by King Balak of Moab to curse Israel.
key: Balak summoned him to curse Israel, and his donkey spoke to stop him (Numbers 22).
Instead of cursing Israel, he blessed them three times (Numbers 23–24).
His advice led Israel into sin with Midian, and he was killed in battle (Numbers 31).
The New Testament names him as an example of greed and false teaching (Revelation 2).

gad_1262.name: Gad
gad_1262.who: Son of Jacob by Leah's servant Zilpah, ancestor of the tribe of Gad.
key: Leah named him Gad, saying good fortune had come (Genesis 30).
He went down to Egypt with Jacob and his sons (Genesis 46).
Jacob blessed him, saying raiders would attack him but he would strike back (Genesis 49).
His tribe settled east of the Jordan, with livestock land in Gilead (Numbers 32).

satan_2476.name: Satan
satan_2476.who: The adversary of God and his people, who tempts, accuses, and deceives, and whose final defeat Scripture foretells.
key: He accused Job before the Lord and was allowed to test him (Job 1–2).
He incited David to take a census of Israel (1 Chronicles 21).
He tempted Jesus in the wilderness, and Jesus resisted him with Scripture (Matthew 4).
He entered Judas, who then betrayed Jesus (Luke 22).
He will be thrown into the lake of fire forever (Revelation 20).

pilate_2365.name: Pontius Pilate
pilate_2365.who: Roman governor of Judea who sentenced Jesus to be crucified.
key: He governed Judea when John the Baptist began his ministry (Luke 3).
He questioned Jesus about being king of the Jews and found no guilt in him (John 18).
He sent Jesus to Herod, then released Barabbas at the crowd's demand (Luke 23).
He washed his hands before the crowd and handed Jesus over to be crucified (Matthew 27).
He allowed Joseph of Arimathea to take Jesus' body for burial (Mark 15).

abner_57.name: Abner
abner_57.who: Son of Ner, Saul's relative and the commander of Saul's army.
key: He was commander of King Saul's army (1 Samuel 14).
After David killed Goliath, Abner brought him to Saul (1 Samuel 17).
He made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king and killed Asahel in battle (2 Samuel 2).
He agreed to bring Israel over to David but was murdered by Joab (2 Samuel 3).

asa_318.name: Asa
asa_318.who: King of Judah, son of Abijah, who removed idols and relied on the Lord for much of his reign.
key: He removed idols and deposed his grandmother Maacah as queen mother (1 Kings 15).
He relied on the Lord and defeated Zerah the Ethiopian's huge army (2 Chronicles 14).
Encouraged by the prophet Azariah, he led Judah to renew the covenant (2 Chronicles 15).
He paid Ben-hadad to attack Israel and was rebuked by Hanani the seer (2 Chronicles 16).
Diseased in his feet, he sought physicians rather than the Lord (2 Chronicles 16).

elisha_1153.name: Elisha
elisha_1153.who: Son of Shaphat, Elijah's successor as prophet in Israel, known for many miracles.
key: Elijah threw his cloak on Elisha while he was plowing, and he followed him (1 Kings 19).
He received a double portion of Elijah's spirit when Elijah was taken up (2 Kings 2).
He multiplied a widow's oil and raised the Shunammite woman's son (2 Kings 4).
He told Naaman the Syrian to wash in the Jordan, and Naaman was healed (2 Kings 5).
At Dothan, God opened his servant's eyes to see an army of fiery chariots (2 Kings 6).

isaiah_617.name: Isaiah
isaiah_617.who: Son of Amoz and prophet in Jerusalem who foretold judgment and the coming Messiah.
key: He saw the Lord enthroned in the temple and was sent to prophesy (Isaiah 6).
He gave King Ahaz the sign of a virgin bearing a son, Immanuel (Isaiah 7).
He assured Hezekiah that God would defend Jerusalem from Assyria (Isaiah 37).
He told the ill Hezekiah God would add fifteen years to his life (Isaiah 38).
He foretold that Hezekiah's treasures would be carried to Babylon (Isaiah 39).

job_1639.name: Job
job_1639.who: A blameless and upright man from Uz who suffered great loss yet did not curse God.
key: Satan was allowed to test him, and he lost his livestock, servants, and children (Job 1).
Struck with painful sores, he refused to curse God (Job 2).
His three friends insisted he must have sinned, and he defended his innocence (Job 4–31).
The Lord answered him out of the whirlwind (Job 38).
He repented, prayed for his friends, and God restored him twice over (Job 42).

baal_573.name: Baal
baal_573.who: A Canaanite false god whose worship repeatedly led Israel into idolatry.

zedekiah_1950.name: Zedekiah
zedekiah_1950.who: Son of Josiah and the last king of Judah before Babylon destroyed Jerusalem.
key: Nebuchadnezzar made him king and changed his name from Mattaniah to Zedekiah (2 Kings 24).
He and Jerusalem's leaders broke their covenant to free their Hebrew slaves (Jeremiah 34).
He secretly consulted Jeremiah but did not obey the word of the Lord (Jeremiah 37–38).
After Jerusalem fell, his sons were killed, and he was blinded and taken to Babylon (Jeremiah 39).

mordecai_2107.name: Mordecai
mordecai_2107.who: Jewish exile of the tribe of Benjamin in Susa who raised his cousin Esther and helped save his people.
key: He raised his orphaned cousin Esther and uncovered a plot against King Ahasuerus (Esther 2).
He refused to bow to Haman, who then plotted to destroy all the Jews (Esther 3).
He urged Esther to plead with the king for her people (Esther 4).
The king honored him for saving his life, with Haman leading the procession (Esther 6).
He was made second to the king and established the feast of Purim (Esther 9–10).

gideon_1314.name: Gideon
gideon_1314.who: Son of Joash and judge of Israel whom God used to deliver Israel from Midian.
key: The angel of the Lord called him while he threshed wheat in a winepress (Judges 6).
He tore down his father's Baal altar and was named Jerubbaal (Judges 6).
He asked God for signs with a fleece before going to battle (Judges 6).
With three hundred men, trumpets, and torches, he routed the Midianite army (Judges 7).
He refused to be king but made a gold ephod that became a snare (Judges 8).

josiah_1730.name: Josiah
josiah_1730.who: Godly king of Judah, son of Amon, who led sweeping reforms after the Book of the Law was found.
key: A man of God foretold by name that Josiah would destroy the altar at Bethel (1 Kings 13).
He became king at eight, and the Book of the Law was found during temple repairs (2 Kings 22).
He renewed the covenant and destroyed idols and high places throughout the land (2 Kings 23).
He kept a great Passover in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 35).
He was killed fighting Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo (2 Chronicles 35).

naphtali_2149.name: Naphtali
naphtali_2149.who: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Naphtali in Galilee.
key: Rachel named him Naphtali after her struggles with her sister (Genesis 30).
Jacob blessed him as a doe let loose (Genesis 49).
His tribe's land in Galilee became a place of Jesus' ministry (Matthew 4).

sarah_2473.name: Sarah
sarah_2473.who: Wife of Abraham who, though barren into old age, bore the promised son Isaac.
key: Abram's wife Sarai was barren and had no child (Genesis 11).
She gave her servant Hagar to Abram to bear a child for her (Genesis 16).
God renamed her Sarah and promised she would bear a son (Genesis 17).
She laughed when she heard she would have a son in her old age (Genesis 18).
At ninety she gave birth to Isaac, as God had promised (Genesis 21).

jehu_817.name: Jehu
jehu_817.who: Army commander anointed king of Israel to destroy the house of Ahab and Baal worship.
key: God told Elijah to anoint Jehu king over Israel (1 Kings 19).
Anointed by a young prophet sent by Elisha, he killed Kings Joram and Ahaziah (2 Kings 9).
At his command, Jezebel was thrown from a window and died (2 Kings 9).
He wiped out Ahab's family and Baal's worshipers but kept Jeroboam's golden calves (2 Kings 10).

noah_2210.name: Noah
noah_2210.who: Righteous man who built the ark and, with his family, survived the flood.
key: In a corrupt world, Noah found favor with the Lord and was told to build an ark (Genesis 6).
He entered the ark with his family and the animals before the flood came (Genesis 7).
After the waters receded, he built an altar and offered sacrifices to the Lord (Genesis 8).
God made a covenant with him, sealed by the rainbow (Genesis 9).
After becoming drunk, he cursed Canaan and blessed Shem and Japheth (Genesis 9).

esther_1343.name: Esther
esther_1343.who: Jewish orphan raised by Mordecai who became queen of Persia and saved her people from destruction.
key: Raised by her cousin Mordecai, she was chosen queen by King Ahasuerus (Esther 2).
Learning of Haman's plot, she asked the Jews to fast before she approached the king (Esther 4).
The king welcomed her, and she invited him and Haman to a banquet (Esther 5).
At a second banquet she exposed Haman's plot, and he was hanged (Esther 7).
She obtained a royal decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves (Esther 8).

laban_1803.name: Laban
laban_1803.who: Rebekah's brother in Haran, father of Leah and Rachel, and Jacob's uncle and father-in-law.
key: He welcomed Abraham's servant and agreed to Rebekah's marriage to Isaac (Genesis 24).
He gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel, then gave Rachel for seven more years (Genesis 29).
He repeatedly changed Jacob's wages while Jacob's flocks increased (Genesis 30–31).
He pursued Jacob, then made a covenant with him at Mizpah (Genesis 31).

zebulun_3002.name: Zebulun
zebulun_3002.who: Sixth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun.
key: He was born to Leah, who hoped her husband would now honor her (Genesis 30).
Jacob blessed him, saying he would dwell at the shore of the sea (Genesis 49).
His tribe was praised for risking their lives in battle under Deborah and Barak (Judges 5).

haman_1360.name: Haman
haman_1360.who: Son of Hammedatha the Agagite, a Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.
key: Promoted by King Ahasuerus, he plotted to kill all Jews when Mordecai would not bow (Esther 3).
On his wife's advice he built a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5).
The king made him lead Mordecai through the city in honor (Esther 6).
Esther exposed his plot, and he was hanged on the gallows he built (Esther 7).
His ten sons were killed when the Jews defended themselves (Esther 9).
